Composite: Getty and Shutterstock Hungary Hide the Pain Harold and Rubik’s Cube creator among social media’s picks for Hungarian president Newly elected Tisza party asked public to put forward names, which have ranged from the sensible to the bizarre Lili Rutai in Budapest Mon 3 Aug 2026 02.10 EDT Last modified on Mon 3 Aug 2026 02.11 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Eszter Jámbor, a 46-year-old content creator who focuses on sex education, had a different kind of question for her Instagram followers last week: who did they think should be Hungary’s next president? The suggestions ranged from reality TV stars to bodybuilders and the Victoria’s Secret model Barbara Palvin. But another anonymous online poll asking Hungarians the same question revealed the most popular candidate to be András Arató, a retired electrical engineer who found global online fame as a meme: Hide the Pain Harold. Katalin Karikó, the Nobel-winning biochemist, and Ernő Rubik, the inventor of the Rubik’s cube, were also popular choices. “Obviously, politics are serious, but there’s also room for a bit of humour, for that sense of freedom that a part of Hungary is now feeling after the past 16 years,” said Jámbor. Since ousting its rightwing populist leader Viktor Orbán in a milestone election earlier this year, the central European country has been living through a period of rapid political change. The man who succeeded Orbán, Péter Magyar , has begun enacting some of the reforms he promised on the campaign trail: taking “propaganda broadcasts” on public media off air and removing Orbán’s allies from the heads of the prosecution, police and military. Perhaps the biggest fight, however, was the one Magyar picked with the then president, Tamás Sulyok, who was forced to sign a constitutional amendment ending his own term in July. After Sulyok, who was appointed by Orbán’s Fidesz party, left his post, the new prime minister called for suggestions. “Let’s make a decision together,” he said in a Facebook video. View image in fullscreen Péter Magyar speaking in front of EU and Hungarian flags. Photograph: Robert Hegedus/MTI/AP Lawmakers from the ruling Tisza party will elect the new president in parliament, but Magyar encouraged “public figures, NGOs and civilians” to put forward names. Less than 24 hours after opening the discussion, however, Magyar said he had nominated the chess grandmaster Judit Polgár for the role. The move prompted a popular backlash criticising his hastiness and Polgár, subject of the Netflix documentary Queen of Chess, turned him down . Magyar apologised for the “miscommunication”, but polls in the aftermath showed his party’s popularity down by 3%. “The process is still imperfect,” says Imre Ónádi, a 55-year-old architect who created a Facebook page and group to support the candidacy of the conservative politician Péter Márki-Zay, who unsuccessfully ran against Orbán in the 2022 general election. Ónádi welcomed Polgár’s refusal “not because she isn’t the right person, but because her nomination was announced without discussion”. He thought Magyar’s apology was a good sign. “It seems they take into account what the population says. That’s democracy, after all,” he added. For now, emboldened by the grassroots success of the Tisza party in the April election but lacking any official channel for recommendations, that discussion is happening in social media posts, online polls and open letters. However, it is unclear whether these popular recommendations are reaching Tisza and how the administration intends to handle them. While the government has set up an online consultation space to discuss an update on traffic regulations, there is no official channel for presidential recommendations, despite Magyar’s encouraging words. “I have a political fever,” said Jámbor, undeterred. “I’ve been voting since I was 18. But I finally feel like I have a say in what happens in the country.” skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every day Sign up to Headlines Europe A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day Preview latest after newsletter promotion ‘Attack on civil society’: why Viktor Orbán’s favourite thinktank is in crisis Read more Any Hungarian over the age of 35 with voting rights can become president, but Magyar has said his candidate must be independent of political parties. He has met two popular contenders: the well-known historian Ignác Romsics and Botond Fülöp, a lawyer who uncovered the child abuse pardon scandal that ended the presidency of Katalin Novák in 2024 . It is expected that Tisza’s 141 parliamentarians will propose and swear in a candidate before 19 August. Technically, Fidesz, which has 44 members of parliament, could nominate its own candidate, but the party has said it will not take part in the election as it believes Sulyok’s dismissal was unlawful. No other party has enough MPs to nominate someone for the position. Amnesty International Hungary believed that the removal of Sulyok was justified, said Áron Demeter, the head of communications and campaigns in the organisation’s Budapest office. “But we could debate Tisza’s method,” he added, arguing that the government could have pursued impeachment to remove the president instead of pushing through an amendment to the constitution. With its so-called supermajority in parliament, Tisza “shouldn’t do the same things Fidesz did, with the same tools, just because their goal is nobler”, Demeter said. (KAKE) – For anyone who drives in Wichita or, really, all throughout Kansas, it can seem that our town and even our cities can shut down for a few minutes … for a train. The Orphan Grain Train operates in the U.S. and the world to ship what people need. It is a non-profit Christian volunteer network and, on its website, reports more than 5,356 semi-trailer truckloads of materials to more than 74 countries and several disaster areas in the U.S. “By far the most common items we send out is used clothing,” said John Evans, with the Wichita office of Orphan Grain Train. “It’s donated; we sort it and, on occasion, it needs repair, we mend it. We will wash it, and we’re real picky. We don’t just send junk over.” Evans shared the story of Reverend Ray Wilke, who went to Latvia in 1992, just after the breakup of the Soviet Union. “A lot of people were hurting,” said Evans. “He came back with a mission to take rail cars around the grain mills, get a load of grain and ship it to Latvia. Certain railroads don’t work that way, and he had to modify it.” That led to a connection in Nebraska to bring in trucks to help gather these basics to ship to Eastern Europe. The costs do add up. “A typical shipment from our location, depends where we go, is between $6,000 and $14,000 so any little bit helps,” said Evans. The call is for donations, but also for muscle to load the shipments. “We absolutely can use volunteers,” said Evans. “The biggest need for volunteers is to help fill a truck. We need quite a few people for that.” GoFundMe Ogt.org Latest Headlines from CNN Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Tags Orphan Grain Train Charity Volunteering Donations Humanitarian Aid Disaster Relief Christian Organization Used Clothing Kansas Community Service Chris Earl Anchor Author facebook Author twitter Author email Follow Chris Earl Close Get email notifications on {{subject}} daily! Skip next section Amit Shah criticizes opposition over 'vote theft' protests 10/22/2026 October 22, 2026 Amit Shah criticizes opposition over 'vote theft' protests Indian Home Minister Amit Shah accused the opposition of using allegations of "vote theft" to challenge the BJP's electoral victories [FILE: July 6, 2026] Image: Naveen Sharma/ANI Union Home Minister Amit Shah criticized Congress and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Thursday over allegations of electoral irregularities , saying protests and demonstrations would not help them win elections, the Hindustan Times reported. Speaking at an event in Delhi, Shah accused the opposition of using allegations of "vote theft" to challenge the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) electoral victories. Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi has claimed that India's election authority had enabled "vote theft," or manipulation of electoral rolls to favor Modi's BJP in the 2024 general elections. Currently, the opposition along with the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other student organizations are demanding the resignation of the country's controversy-hit Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar , after more than 130 million names were removed from draft electoral rolls nationwide. Meanwhile, separately, BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia accused Gandhi of links with foreign-based organizations that he alleged were amplifying protests in India, the Times of India newspaper reported. Bhatia alleged that the organizations were part of a wider effort to create unrest and undermine constitutional institutions, and demanded that Gandhi disclose details of his meetings with them, the report said. https://p.dw.com/p/5OXqs Skip next section One Indian killed, three injured in attacks on Saudi airport, oilfield 10/22/2026 October 22, 2026 One Indian killed, three injured in attacks on Saudi airport, oilfield One Indian national was killed and two others injured in an attack on Dammam airport in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, while another Indian national was injured in an attack on the Shaybah oil field, the Indian foreign ministry said in a statement on Thursday. The Wednesday evening attack in the Saudi Arabian city of Dammam killed two people and eight others in total, the country's aviation authority said on Thursday. In a separate attack on Wednesday, two people were killed by debris from an intercepted drone launched by the Iran-backed Houthis targeting the Shaybah oil field operated by state energy giant Aramco, Saudi media reported. The US embassy in Riyadh issued a security alert on Wednesday about possible further attacks by the Houthis on Saudi Arabia. "We strongly condemn the continued attacks on civilian and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, including the attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oil field in the Eastern Province on October 21," the Indian foreign ministry statement said. "These attacks have unfortunately resulted in civilian deaths and injuries," India's foreign ministry said. Can Yemen's government turn the tide against the Houthis? "Our growing economic strength has created new opportunities for the India-Poland partnership. And the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement has made these opportunities even broader," Modi said while addressing the joint press meet with Tusk. Tusk said the friendship between New Delhi and Warsaw is not based merely on diplomatic relations, but on the "shared heritage of humanity and empathy." The two leaders oversaw the exchange of several memorandums of understanding. Tusk is on a two-day trip to India ending on Friday. He is accompanied by Polish Minister of Finance and Economy, Andrzej Domanski, and a business delegation . On Wednesday, Tusk met Indian Foreign Minister S Jaishankar where the two discussed ways to deepen bilateral cooperation, according to reports. This comes even as three more people were arrested in connection with the shooting, Mumbai Police said. The total number of people arrested related to the case has now risen to 10. Three motorcycle-borne assailants had opened fire at Shroff's car in the western city of Mumbai on October 18. The actor escaped unhurt, while his driver and a bystander were injured. Three key accused, including the alleged shooters, were caught by the police while trying to escape to Nepal. Police suspect the attack was carried out at the behest of Anil Pandit, an alleged operative of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang . The Bishnoi gang , accused of involvement in the 2023 killing of Sikh separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada, has claimed responsibility for the attack. Bishnoi, a jailed Indian gangster, has been accused by US prosecutors of directing murders, extortion and international drug trafficking from inside a prison in Gujarat. https://p.dw.com/p/5OXM7 Skip next section Google, Mozilla, Apple block certificates by Indian company over security flaw 10/22/2026 October 22, 2026 Google, Mozilla, Apple block certificates by Indian company over security flaw The cybersecurity flaw could have allowed attackers to impersonate legitimate websites using fraudulent certificates [December 14, 2025] Image: Philip Dulian/dpa/picture alliance Bengaluru-based digital identity and cybersecurity company eMudhra has revoked eight intermediate certificates after their private keys were found to be weak, prompting Google , Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft to block the affected certificates. "Eight intermediate (issuing) CAs in our Global TLS business were revoked because their published keys were weak," the company said, adding that it was investigating the issue. A certificate authority (CA) is an organization that browsers such as Chrome, Firefox and Safari rely on to verify website identities and establish secure connections. The flaw could have allowed attackers to impersonate legitimate websites using fraudulent certificates and potentially intercept or manipulate supposedly secure online communications. However, no evidence of such misuse has been publicly confirmed. The flaw originated in a key-generation process in April 2025 that produced weak private keys, the company said . Media reports citing security researcher Scott Helme said one of the keys was the number four, rather than a cryptographically secure, randomly generated number, while others were also easily guessable. India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) said it had taken serious note of the incident. "A special team has been constituted to investigate the matter," the ministry said in a statement on X. https://p.dw.com/p/5OX3X Skip next section CJP leaders freed after undertaking not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar 10/22/2026 October 22, 2026 CJP leaders freed after undertaking not to call for protests at Jantar Mantar Das and Ranka have been seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over voter-roll irregularities Image: Sanchit Khanna/Hindustan Times/IMAGO Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released from Tihar Jail on Wednesday after a Special Executive Magistrate declined a police request to extend their judicial custody by three more days, reports said. The two leaders at the forefront of the protests calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar following voter-list irregularities, furnished personal bonds and sureties of Rs 50,000 (€470; $530) each. Their written undertakings promised to maintain peace and not call for protests at Jantar Mantar "till such a time that it is denotified in accordance with law." The iconic protest site was denotified by Delhi Police earlier in October, months after CJP-led protests culminated in the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Das and Ranka were booked for "trespassing" after entering the Jantar Mantar protest site and raising the Indian flag.
